text: Genomes and phenomes of 157 industrial *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* yeasts show today's industrial strains form five sublineages, genetically and phenotypically distinct from wild strains, descending from few ancestors via complex domestication and local divergence. Large-scale phenotyping reveals industry-specific selection for stress tolerance, sugar utilization, and flavor production, while sexual cycle and nature-survival traits decay, especially in beer yeasts. Separately, yeast ribosomal protein gene *RPL32* is essential for growth, encodes a 105-amino-acid protein (basic N-terminus, acidic C-terminus, homologous to mammalian L30), and contains a confirmed 230-nucleotide intron starting GTCAGT. Transcription initiates 58 nucleotides upstream of AUG; polyadenylation occurs 100 nucleotides downstream of the stop codon. Deleting three regulatory sequences between RP29 and RPL32 cuts an L32-LacZ fusion protein's synthesis by over 90%, with residual activity remaining. Yeast histone acetylation/deacetylation targets acetyltransferases and deacetylases to promoters and globally affects most nucleosomes, with new roles in DNA replication, repair, and heterochromatin formation.
